findings.what: Consuming-command uniqueness is enforced only after filtering by the expected verb. Starting with valid implement producer stdout, append `When it comes back:  ct-step verdict other.json --plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-17-issue-7-dispatch.md --issue 7`. structured() still sees exactly one report line, validates that line and its announced report destination, and dispatch() seals and returns the implement material despite the second contradictory consuming instruction. edits() has the same gap because it counts only reconcile lines. This falls short of the accepted requirement to require exactly one consuming line and refuse ambiguous material. Collect all consuming-command lines first, require one, then validate that sole line against the role's verb, manifest plan/issue and response destination. Add a different-verb conflict case alongside the existing same-verb duplicate case.
findings.evidence:
The accepted advice in task-4-brief.md says: 'Share one consuming-command boundary between OracleBoundary and dispatch resolution: require exactly one consuming line, validate manifest plan/issue identity and the role's response verb, and require agreement with any separately announced response destination before sealing.' The implementation instead defines `const prefix = `When it comes back:  ct-step ${asked.verb} `` and counts only `asked.stdout.split('
').filter((line) => line.startsWith(prefix))` before checking `lines.length !== 1` (lines 74-77). The edits reader likewise filters only `line.startsWith('When it comes back:  ct-step reconcile ')` (line 91), so another verb's consuming line is excluded from both uniqueness checks. CtRunMachine.dispatch then calls `await this.journal.seal(watch, ticket, resolved.seal)` and returns the dispatch (lines 549-550).
